rule: Operator directive 2026-09-12: every guide image must cross-reference public Apple/reference imaging down to the smallest observable detail; the same strict ruleset applies to every plate; details are baked, tracked, logged and audited before any render. Chat-only operator photos (not persisted to sandbox disk) are recorded in refs.chatOnly with full perception receipts and MUST be re-uploaded before they can be passed as image references.
naming: simple descriptive kebab names, no token ceremony

images.subject: Memory instruction infographic printed on the inside/back of the removable Mac Pro 3,1 access panel - OPERATOR'S PRIMARY STYLE+VIEW REFERENCE ('perfectly represents my vision')
images.source: operator chat attachment 2026-09-12 (arena attachment; not written to sandbox disk - /home/user/uploads absent). Re-upload required to pass as image reference.
details: brushed silver aluminum panel background, black ink only, photographed at an angle with glare (glare is photo artifact, never art)
artwork left half: the Mac Pro tower shell shown lying on its back/open side, THREE-QUARTER PERSPECTIVE (~20-30 degree angled view from above and front), not flat orthographic
tower outline includes the signature one-piece top handle cutout and rounded stand/foot shapes at both frame ends

front mesh face is visible on the left of the shell with perforation stippling and the two long horizontal optical-slot trim bars one above the other, plus a vertical column of small port/button glyphs below them

memory compartment at the open face: TWO flat rectangular riser carrier plates drawn pulled straight OUT, perpendicular from the logic board plane, each plate carrying a row of upright DIMM outlines (3 to 4 per plate) with clips
UPPER carrier plate has a bold letter 'A' at its outer right corner; LOWER carrier plate has a bold letter 'B' at its outer right corner
the in-cage seated positions of both plates are drawn inside the shell; pulled-out plates are solid outline slightly offset, no heavy ghosting style but clearly detached
TWO solid black filled block arrows with triangular heads point horizontally outward from the open face, one per plate, showing straight pull direction

right half text block, top to bottom: 'IMPORTANT' in bold; English 'To install memory, see the user's guide.'; French 'Pour installer de la memoire, consultez le guide de l utilisateur.'; German 'Anleitungen zum Installieren von Speicher finden Sie im Benutzerhandbuch' (line cropped at right edge); Spanish 'Para instalar memoria, consulte la guia del usuario.'; fifth line is the Japanese translation of the same sentence (described only, NOT reproduced anywhere in our English-only guide art)

the five-language IMPORTANT text is recorded for fidelity to the reference but guide plates render ENGLISH ONLY per contract; the sticker's black-line + filled-block-arrow + three-quarter shell language is what gets copied, not its foreign text
line weights are uniform and thin, outline-only, no shading, no gray fill, no gradients - stippling used for the mesh grille only
composition is spacious: one chassis, one action, generous whitespace; the text occupies its own clean column and never overlaps the art

viewpoint target for the guide: same angled shell on its side; removed parts exit straight toward the viewer/open side with a single bold arrow; removed/next-state part may be dashed at 40% per contract but the solid arrow language is identical

images.subject: Apple 'Memory Riser Card Replacement Instructions' page 1 for Mac Pro (Early 2008)
images.source: Apple 073-1180 Rev. A, via yumpu document 55991164
details: white page, black Apple logo + 'Mac Pro' wordmark top right, thin horizontal rule under header
large two-line sans-serif title, generous leading; numbered steps left column, black numerals
Warning callouts use a round-triangle caution icon with internal exclamation mark, bold 'Warning:' lead-in
no imagery on page 1 beyond header art: typographic restraint is the style signal
footer: copyright left, document number '073-1180 Rev. A' and page number right
defines the canonical typographic voice: sentence case instructions, short numbered actions, one action per number

images.subject: Apple 'PCIe/Graphics Card Replacement Instructions' page 1 (073-1248 Rev. A, 2009 sheet, same chassis family and art language)
images.source: Apple 073-1248 Rev. A, via yumpu document 55991451
details: two rounded-corner illustration panels stacked vertically, each with a light blue gradient background and thin black border
the tower is drawn in THREE-QUARTER PERSPECTIVE matching the panel sticker: top handle cutout, rounded feet, front mesh face with optical slot bars, side access panel
a skin-toned hand and forearm show the exact grip/press action (our BW contract renders hands outline-only, no skin tone)
numbered action badges: black numeral on yellow-to-red radial circle with white outer ring, placed at the action point with a curved red-yellow motion arrow
panel 1: finger presses the latch area at the rear of the side panel; power cord still plugged during static discharge step
panel 2: badge 1 at the rear latch lifting up, large curved arrow badge 2 showing the side panel swinging/lifting away

chassis proportions in this art: tall rectangular body, handle spans nearly full width at top, front face mesh suggested with fine dot stipple, optical drive faceplates as two slim horizontal rounded rectangles
the Apple logo on the removable side panel is centered and rendered at low gray (outline only in our BW contract)

images.subject: Mac Pro (Early 2008) interior with side panel removed, case on its side (Memory Cage with Rear Fan guide establishing shot)
images.source: iFixit guide 25939 'Memory Cage with Rear Fan (Early 2008) Replacement' step 1 image 1
details: case lying on its side, open face filling frame; rounded top handle spans upper edge, stand foot lower edge

TOP ZONE (case-on-side): left optical carrier is a wide smooth aluminum plate with TWO small rounded-rectangle cutouts side by side, each cutout has one tiny dark screw dot at its lower edge; right optical carrier is one large plain smooth plate
MIDDLE ZONE: four identical silver HDD blank/sled faceplates in a horizontal row separated by narrow black gaps, each with a small raised/oval feature near top edge and tiny screws

CENTER-RIGHT ZONE: logic board visible - blue PCB, dense cylindrical electrolytic caps with light tops, a large black finned processor heatsink lying horizontally, smaller heatsinks, a small BLACK RECTANGULAR MODULE highlighted by a yellow rectangle in the source annotation (annotation not part of hardware)
LOWER-LEFT ZONE: one large smooth silver memory-cage shroud/cover with rounded corner, fully blank (it hides riser A/B until removed)

LOWER-RIGHT ZONE: rectangular windowed cage exposing TWO memory riser banks stacked one above the other; each bank shows white/heatsinked FB-DIMMs in vertical clips flanked by green PCB and purple/lavender cylindrical caps at the board edges
RIGHT EDGE: silver locking latch lever angled outward mid-height; honeycomb/dot vent perforations along inner frame edges
all zones are separated by clean aluminum frame rails; no cables visible across the open face in factory state

counts that must never drift in guide art: optical carriers = 2 (left dual-cutout, right plain); HDD faces = exactly 4; riser banks visible = 2; cutouts on left optical carrier = 2 each with screw dot

images.subject: Official Apple user-guide line drawing: Mac Pro rear panel left and right port layouts with leader labels
images.source: Apple Mac Pro (Early 2008) User Guide rear-panel illustration (same art used for 2006-2008 Mac Pro guides)
details: two rear three-quarter views of the tower side by side on pure white, black outline + dot stipple, no fill
mesh grille rendered as uniform fine dot stipple; solid aluminum panels stay white
top of rear face: square IEC power socket with the small square locking latch directly above/beside it
upper-middle: five horizontal slatted PCI expansion slot covers in a framed rectangular block
left of PCI block a long vertical slim grille/vent column
lower-left: large CIRCULAR perforated speaker/fan grille drawn as a packed dot circle

lower-right I/O cluster: two stacked RJ-45 Gigabit Ethernet jacks, FireWire 800 (9-pin) and FireWire 400 (6-pin) ports, three USB 2.0 ports, optical digital audio in and out (mini-TOSLINK circles), analog audio line-in and line-out paired jacks
labels are set in a plain sans-serif face with thin straight leader lines ending at each port; leader lines never cross each other
this is the authoritative stipple-and-leader style for any port/back-panel plate

images.subject: Mac Pro 3,1 memory riser card 820-2178-04 with FB-DIMMs installed, showing ejectors, finger holes and heatsink clips
images.source: iFixit guide 25937 'Memory (FB-DIMMs) and Memory Riser Cards (Early 2008) Replacement' step 7
details: blue riser PCB with large gold card-edge connector along the full bottom edge
TWO large round finger holes, one at each end of the riser board (these are what the DIY sheet means by 'holding the riser by the two finger holes')
silkscreen on board reads 'APPLE 820-2178-04' with copyright 2007; a white asset sticker and a pink 'S659' tag appear in the source photo (do not draw tags in guide art)
FOUR FB-DIMM slots; populated DIMMs carry thick black finned heatsinks with a thin green PCB edge visible
each FB-DIMM is retained by THREE silver metal spring clips spanning the heatsink plus black plastic ejector levers at both board ends
two rows of purple/lavender cylindrical capacitors run across the board behind the slots, plus smaller silver caps
ghosted second riser behind shows the second bank of slots - the two risers are mechanically identical
yellow source arrows point at ejectors and clips (annotations, not hardware)
DIMMs mount VERTICALLY to the riser; the riser itself mounts horizontally into the cage when the case is on its side

images.subject: Mac Pro Early 2008 A1186 marketing composite: front three-quarter view, access panel, and rear panel
images.source: apple.techable.com Mac Pro 2008 Eight Core 2.8 GHz MA970LL/A A1186 EMC 2180 page
details: FRONT: full-height perforated aluminum mesh face with dense round hole pattern across the entire front plane
two long horizontal optical slot bezels stacked in the upper third, rounded ends, spanning most of the face width
center I/O strip below the slots: circular power button at top, headphone/optical audio hole, two stacked USB ports, one FireWire 800 and one FireWire 400 port, all in a slim recessed vertical column
the one-piece aluminum carry handle forms a wide rectangular loop across the full top with open grip gap beneath
the bottom stand is a wide curved aluminum foot with open cutouts; front corners of the body are softly rounded where the handle hoop and foot meet

ACCESS PANEL (top-right in composite): flat aluminum door with a large centered faint Apple logo and a small square latch/handle cutout near one edge; bottom corners have notched standoffs that hook into the frame
REAR (small inset): mesh lower face, circular speaker grille, IEC socket top, five horizontal PCI slot covers, I/O cluster bottom-right exactly matching apple-rear-ports-lineart
body side profile is a simple tall rounded rectangle with slight taper; there are NO front-facing drive doors - HDD bays are internal, invisible from the front

images.subject: HDD sled being inserted into the drive bay row, hand supporting the aluminum faceplate
images.source: iFixit guide 65551 'Hard Drive Sled Adapter for Mac Pro First Generation' step 4
details: sled faceplate is a plain brushed aluminum rectangle with a SMALL CIRCLED NUMBER ('1') at its lower-right corner - bays are numbered on the sleds/frame
behind the faceplate the black plastic/metal drive carrier is visible with the 3.5 inch drive mounted, connector end facing inward
the bay opening exposes green PCB (drive backplane) at the inner top edge and silver guide rails
adjacent bays to the right show empty vertical rail slots with the same circled numbers 1/2/3 running down a label strip (upright orientation)
motion is straight IN toward the backplane on rails, supported from underneath - never tilted, no screws turned to insert, the captive thumbscrew secures it afterward
the faceplate sits nearly flush with the four-bay aluminum row when seated; above it the optical carrier screw dots are visible

canonicalFacts: machine Mac Pro 3,1 Early 2008, A1186 family, EMC 2180, MacPro3,1; two FB-DIMM risers A (top/upside-down) and B (bottom), four slots each, 8 total

case-on-side open-face zones top-to-bottom of the open face: 2 optical carriers -> 4 HDD sled faces -> board/cage zone -> memory shroud (left) + riser window (right); rear latch lever on the right frame edge
chassis drawn in the panel-sticker three-quarter view on every plate; only scale and highlighted action change between plates

counts are invariants: 2 optical carriers, 2 optical cutouts on the left carrier with screw dots, 4 HDD bays, 4 screws/rail features per sled, 2 risers x 4 DIMMs, 2 riser finger holes per board, 5 PCI slot covers, 2 GbE + FW400 + FW800 + 3 USB at the rear cluster, one IEC socket, one latch

removal language copied from the panel sticker: removed carrier slides straight out perpendicular to the board, shown detached beside its opening with one solid black block arrow; seated state drawn solid, detached state dashed at 40%

typography copied from Apple DIY sheets: Helvetica, sentence case, short numbered action steps, bold IMPORTANT/WARNING lead-ins, caution triangle icon; guide plates keep short labels only per text budget
